Strait of Hormuz Status: October 10, 2026 | Straits Daily Brief
Skip to content Straits Hormuz Live Monitor Day  224 Open? Live map News About Method API Live

Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
10 October 2026 .
Brent $ 104.72 + 0.42 % · Transits 4 (2026-10-04) · AI-assisted
01 WANA News Agency reports the IRGC says an oil tanker caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz after striking a sea mine; UAE authorities rescued 22 crew members.

02 IMF PortWatch recorded 4 transits on October 4, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day.

03 Brent settled at $104.72 at Friday's close, up 0.42% on the session; futures are shut.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed to routine commercial traffic, with the latest incident reported Saturday: the IRGC says an oil tanker caught fire after striking a sea mine, per Saba and WANA News Agency, while gCaptain reports UAE authorities rescued 22 Asian crew members following the blaze. Iranian state media, citing the IRGC, described the vessel as a supertanker that exploded after hitting a mine on an unauthorized transit route; that characterization originates with Iranian state media and should be read as a claim. IMF PortWatch recorded 4 transits on October 4, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day; that figure reflects PortWatch's weekly publication cycle and is not a same-day reading. ABC News reports that shipping companies are now offering sailors sharply elevated pay to transit the strait, a signal of how severely crew risk premiums have risen. Brent settled at $104.72 at Friday's close, up 0.42% on the session; futures are shut and the figure has not moved since close. Talks between Iran and Washington remain deadlocked over sequencing, with Tehran insisting its seven conditions be met before further steps. As of 21:20 UTC, 134 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the high band, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
